thread:
marco: quick note, saw a consistent p99 gap across regions when mixing short+long sequences under q8. opening thread to collect ideas and a rollout plan.
perf-bot: perf run https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/2002001234 (id 2002001234) artifacts -> https://dash.redwood.ai/artifacts/2002001234/
jin: what are the headline numbers?
marco: steady-state: flashv3 p50=12ms p95=35ms p99=90ms. triton p50=10ms p95=38ms p99=210ms. throughput(seq512): flashv3 390 rps, triton 490 rps. note: tail matters for SLOs.
anya: interesting tradeoff. flashv3 wins tail but loses some throughput. is this only on H100?
marco: mainly H100 and some A100 gen2. vendor kernels (triton) sometimes pull ahead for tiny seqs under 64.
sophie: do we have flame graphs or kernel timelines? are we seeing kernel launch storms or CUDA syncs?
perf-bot: flame graphs uploaded: https://dash.redwood.ai/artifacts/2002001234/flame.zip
kyle: my hypothesis: triton batches more eagerly which increases aggregate throughput, but when a long request arrives it forces extra workspace allocations + kernel context changes -> tail spikes.
jin: replicated locally with seq-mix 70/30 short/long and saw per-kernel alloc churn on triton. flashv3 uses contiguous packing that avoids repeated allocs.
marco: q8 adds complexity: temp buffers for dequant+reorder are allocated/deallocated per-call in triton path. flashv3's q8 path reuses workspace and is more incremental.
anya: operational question: what rule should we use per-region to pick default kernel? we need an automated decision + manual override.
kyle: propose metricized decision: compare two control metrics over a 10m window: (A) p99_prefill relative improvement = (triton_p99 - flash_p99)/triton_p99, (B) throughput delta = (flash_thr / triton_thr - 1).
- if A >= 0.30 and B >= -0.12 -> choose flashv3 (favor tail improvement up to 12% throughput loss)
- if B >= 0.20 and A <= 0.10 -> choose triton (throughput wins)
- else keep current kernel and run focused microbench.
sophie: add quality check: if q8 vs fp16 eval shows >0.5% accuracy regression for core prompts -> block automatic switch.
marco: good call. also add sample size floor: at least 1000 requests and >=5m observation.
ops-bot: flag: region eu-west experienced a 0.2% increase in client errors when triton p99 > 180ms last night. recommended canary.
anya: rollout playbook suggestion: canary plan + cooldown + auto-revert. share snippet for infra:
```
canary_plan:
  steps: [10,30,100]
  min_duration: 15m
  metrics:
    p99_threshold_pct: -15   # prefer flashv3 when p99 reduces by 15% or more
    error_rate_max: 0.5%    # rollback if exceeded
    quality_regression_max: 0.5% # from eval set
  hysteresis: 10m
  revert_on: [p99_increase: +10%, error_rate: >0.5%, quality_regression: >0.5%]
```
jin: I'll run a battery of synthetic tracers: seq mixes (90/10, 70/30, 50/50), q8 vs fp16, and short-only baseline. tagging runs with `seqmix-q8-sanity-2002001234`.
perf-bot: scheduled runs: 2002001300, 2002001450, 2002002600. results ETA 2h.
kyle: mitigation when keeping triton: add a light warmup microbatcher that pre-executes a prefill of 8 tokens for the hot model instance when burst detected. cheap and reduces launch penalty.
sophie: we should also record memory transient metrics. flashv3's reuse helps with memory pressure, reducing OOMs on smaller A100 SKUs.
marco: ops request: define per-region default preference and an override owner. I propose: us-east -> flashv3 (bursty traffic), eu-west -> triton (throughput-heavy), apac -> default triton but canary flashv3 for spikes. owners: infra+ml-platform.
anya: final decision criteria for immediate patch: prefer flashv3 when p99 improvement >=30% AND throughput loss <=10% AND no quality regression >0.5% over eval set. otherwise maintain triton and schedule warmup experiment.
deploy-bot: created canary rollout in us-east (10% flashv3) monitor window 30m.
perf-bot: run complete: flashv3 p99=95ms triton p99=205ms; q8 mem drop ~26% but p50 jitter +1.5ms. detailed CSV: https://dash.redwood.ai/artifacts/2002001234/results.csv
jin: uploading kernel timelines and mem histograms. will attach eval prompts comparison soon.
marco: action items: 1) jin: finish eval & attach quality diff (EOD) 2) infra: implement metricized decision & canary snippet (2d) 3) ops: monitor canary and be ready to rollback.
anya: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the 30m canary window.
marco: TL;DR: flashv3 reduces tail substantially in mixed seq traces at modest throughput cost; default per-region decision should account for burstiness, throughput sensitivity, and q8 quality impact.
anya: love it.
